limitations: No measured local cavity/source/noise envelope is certified here.
Finite Gaussian covariance results assume their declared texture and baseline covariance.
The raw-noise oracle theorem is general; the scenario tables use a finite spectral model, not qualified raw telemetry.
Dynamic far-field extrapolation remains an explicit input assumption.
Sampled frequency/direction results do not exclude narrow unsampled resonances or other excitations.
The statistical target is illustrative; failing it does not prove all archaeological utility is zero.

depth_oracle.status: P2-29 solver kernels; the class admits rooms spread 15 m down (dilute superposition checked)

finding: Loose but simple, and with the common background included, the finite certificate caps any processor's detection rate at 5.0172% at 5% false alarms under the regional microseism envelope (detection minus false alarm at most 1.72e-04; P2-25's tighter bound, reference covariance I: 1.3e-09). Every static row excludes 95% at 5%. Of P2-26's dynamic rows, computed with the reference covariance taken as the identity, the largest is the thin-roof room under a truck-level harmonic, at most 23.5% at 5%; but those are a restricted surrogate, not certificates: the no-cavity world already moves with the truck, its covariance is not the identity, and the regional background's floor does not cover it; adding the lorry's own phase energy over the scene, the singular-value argument gives no floor at all (the square roots sum to 1.14 to 1.41, above 1). Under strong shaking the valid bound here is P2-29's oracle with receiver noise. An arbitrary phase modulation within the background envelope on 52,600 pixels is capped at 9.35%; on the whole image the certificate is uninformative. Depth: P2-29's spread rooms 15 m down leave 71% of a room 30 m down's mark unmatched, so where detection just reaches 95% at 5% Theorem E's floor on any method's mean depth error between the two is only 1.8 m of their 15 m separation: in this model the mark's shape carries depth.
